acceptanceCriteria: New TSA-V0 requirements define BLOCK-NOT-CALLED: trigger forms, non-flagged forms (&block forwarded, block.call, yield, instance_exec(&block)), helper + caller reporting, abstention
testsource.ValidityFindings reports BLOCK-NOT-CALLED for the #1140 example helper and each calling example, with path:line for helper and callers
Negative tests: forwarded &block, block.call, yield, instance_exec(&block), and a helper that calls the block on every path are not flagged
testvalidity.ApplySourceFindings maps the rule to an invalid projection with its own reason; spec-requirements-check and focused testsource/testvalidity tests pass
body: GitHub #1140. A spec helper that declares a block parameter (&block, or yield/block_given?) and passes a literal block to an assertion (assert_no_*, assert_*_difference, expect { }, perform_enqueued_jobs, ...) whose body only references the block (bare `block`, `block.itself`) instead of calling it (`block.call`, `yield`, `instance_exec(&block)`), or never calls the block on any path, makes every example using it vacuous. test-validity does not flag this today. Same family as MEMOIZED-BLOCK-EXPECTATION (TSA-V0-049..051, internal/testsource/validity_rspec.go, internal/testvalidity/source_rules.go). Add rule BLOCK-NOT-CALLED (severity invalid) to the RSpec reader with new TSA-V0 requirements in docs/specs/test-source-analysis-v0.md. Report the helper definition and every example in the same file that calls it. `&block` forwarded straight to the assertion (`assert_no_enqueued_jobs(&block)`) must not be flagged. Abstention follows TSA-V0-050.
title: test-validity: BLOCK-NOT-CALLED rule for RSpec helpers that pass a block to an assertion without calling it (GitHub #1140)
